LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: ARABIC ALPHABET

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.1: Guided writing: Arabic Alphabet
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided writing: Arabic Alphabet, part of Writing in Grade 4 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why are greetings important? 2. How does good handwriting look like?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. trace the Arabic symbols and characters of the alphabet neatly,

2. re-write the symbols neatly and legibly,

3. complete words with missing letters (nuun,raa,saad,faa,) with its vowels,

4. team up to prepare a chart on Arabic characters and display on the language corner,

5. copy words on greetings and introductions from a given display. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. trace the Arabic symbols and characters of the alphabet neatly,
2. re-write the symbols neatly and legibly,
3. complete words with missing letters (nuun,raa,saad,faa,) with its vowels,
4. team up to prepare a chart on Arabic characters and display on the language corner,
5. copy words on greetings and introductions from a given display. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided writing: Arabic Alphabet together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: This is promoted as the learner explores possible views when completing words with

missing letters (nuun,raa,saad,faa,) with its vowels.

Values:
Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner engages in assigned duties when teaming up to prepare a chart on Arabic

characters and display on the language corner.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is promoted as the learner embraces the Arabic language by understanding and exploring ways of representing

Arabic characters in writing.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate the concept of Alphabets and symbols to their learning of letters and sounds in English and

Kiswahili.
